Jordan — thanks for the redline. Quick answers below and attached our standard PO sample (Novaclinic_PO_Sample.pdf).

1) Billing entity: For this initial commercial we expect Novaclinic Europe BV to sign and pay (EMEA spend). We may later route US customers through Novaclinic US, Inc. but that is a separate order. For EMEA please route invoices to AP-Europe (ap-eu@novaclinic.com).

2) VAT: We are VAT-registered in the Netherlands. For Redwood services we typically apply reverse-charge (customer liable) — we will provide VAT number on signature. However, our tax team requested an explicit clause in the order form that follows local reverse-charge guidance and a field for supplier VAT ID.

3) PO: We will issue a PO and prefer PO displayed on each invoice; PO will be provided before signature. Our procurement lead (Tom) will confirm the PO number and PO contact.

One more item: our tax team asked if Redwood can accept a staged prepay (50% on signature, remaining billed monthly). Is that configurable on your side?

Jordan / team — I reviewed the draft and Elena’s note. High-level legal positions below; I’ve attached a marked-up version with inline language (Legal_Markup_OrderForm.docx).

- VAT/Reversed-charge: we can include a reverse-charge placeholder but cannot accept broad indemnities that allocate all VAT risk to Redwood. Suggested compromise: include a VAT responsibility clause that defaults to customer where legal/regulation requires reverse charge, and require customer to provide VAT IDs and any supporting certificates.

- Invoicing & split: drafting a tri-party invoicing clause where we can issue: (a) prepay invoice to the signing entity on signature, (b) consumption invoices either to the same entity or to a designated AP mailbox. We need clarity on which legal entity accepts the prepay invoice — that entity will be the obligor for the prepay amount.

- Minimum commit language: the order form currently ties the minimum commit to a single entity; if Novaclinic wants to split commit across two legal entities we need explicit allocation lines in the pricing schedule and a fallback if one entity defaults. I recommend: primary allocation + recovery path (e.g., remaining balance due from parent or consolidated entity) rather than prorating across unidentified accounts.

- Net terms: Net45 is Redwood standard. We can consider Net60 for EU entities for established customers but need Finance sign-off (Mina) and a credit review.

Ben / Mina — please confirm if Finance can accept Net60 for EU and whether prepay of 50% on signature + monthly consumption invoices is supported operationally.

Kimberly Park

Team — quick ops feasibility from Finance & Billing. I modeled three scenarios in the attached spreadsheet (Invoice_Scenario_3.xlsx). TL;DR: we can support the prepay + monthly consumption split and a per-entity invoicing mapping, with caveats:

- Net terms: Our default is Net45. For EU entities we can extend to Net60 on a case-by-case basis after credit verification and completion of tax residency evidence (VAT ID). If Novaclinic provides a VAT ID and confirms reverse-charge treatment, we would not collect VAT on the invoice but will need the VAT number on the invoice and in our system.

- Prepay: 50% prepay on signature is operationally straightforward. We will generate an upfront invoice to the signing legal entity. The remaining 50% can be invoiced monthly against actual consumption or tranches as agreed.

- Invoice splitting: We need the billing contact and a single AP mailbox for delivery of invoices. If Novaclinic requires split invoicing to multiple legal entities within one deal, we need explicit line-item allocations in the pricing schedule (example in sheet).

Action items for Elena/Tom: please provide VAT ID for Novaclinic Europe BV and confirm AP mailbox and whether PO number will be present on each invoice. Also confirm if Novaclinic requires any specific remittance details (bank account / currency preference) for EU payments.

Thanks — Mina
